stem: A parol has red, green and blue lights. The red lights blink every 4 seconds, the green every 6 seconds and the blue every 10 seconds. All three blink together now. After how many seconds will all three next blink together?
hints: The lights repeat, and you want the first time they all meet again. Use the LCM.
List multiples of the biggest number, 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, …
Check each multiple of 10: can it also be divided by 4 and by 6? The first one that passes both is your answer.

solution.methodName: LCM for things that repeat and meet again

steps.action: Things that repeat and meet again call for the LCM of 4, 6 and 10.

steps.why: Start with the biggest number, so there are fewer numbers to check.

steps.action: 10, 30 and 50 cannot be divided by 4 (they leave remainder 2), so they fail.
20 and 40 can be divided by 4, but not by 6, so they fail.
60 ÷ 4 = 15 and 60 ÷ 6 = 10. Both are whole numbers, so the LCM is 60.
All three lights next blink together after 60 seconds.

trapNotes.20: This adds 4 + 6 + 10. At 20 seconds the green lights are not blinking, because 20 ÷ 6 is not a whole number.
trapNotes.120: All three do blink together at 120 seconds, but they already did at 60 seconds. The question asks for the next time.
trapNotes.240: This multiplies 4 × 6 × 10. They do blink together then, but 60 seconds comes much earlier. Use the least common multiple.
